Chapter 10: Living a Life That Leaves a Mark.
You know, deep down, we all want our lives to count. We want to feel like we matter—that what we do actually makes a difference. Most of us picture that impact as something big, maybe even public. But what if I told you the most lasting influence usually comes from the little things, the steady acts of love we show every day?
I’m reminded of a coach I once knew. He spent years working with kids who struggled to believe in themselves. He wasn’t some celebrity, and his teams didn’t exactly rack up the wins. But here’s what’s amazing—years later, those kids came back to say thank you. Not for trophies or championships, but for how he believed in them. For his encouragement, and for the way he was always there when it counted.
Most folks tend to underestimate just how powerful consistency can be. We look for quick results, or hope for some dramatic change overnight. But the most meaningful impact? It’s usually slow—built over time, one steady, faithful moment after another.
Let me share another story. Picture a busy workplace, where one person makes it a habit to notice everyone—the janitor, the receptionist, even the newest hire. They remember birthdays, check in about families, offer a quick word of encouragement. Over time, something subtle but powerful happens. The whole atmosphere shifts. People feel noticed, valued, and inspired to give their best. No, it’s not about profits or awards. It’s about helping people feel like they truly belong.
Living a life that leaves a mark isn’t about being flawless or extraordinary. It’s about showing up, day after day, and choosing to love in those small, everyday ways. It’s about trusting that each act of kindness, no matter how tiny, actually matters.
Most of us will never see the full impact of what we do. The seeds we plant today? They might not bloom for years—or maybe we’ll never see them at all. But that doesn't mean they’re pointless. What really became clear is this: the legacy of love gets built one moment at a time, through the quiet, ordinary choices we make over a lifetime.
